detailed_description: Photographic character reference sheet of ONE character, <Subject 1> EXACTLY FIVE PANELS arranged in three columns. The LEFT TWO COLUMNS contain four equally sized headshot panels in TWO ROWS OF TWO. The RIGHTMOST COLUMN contains ONE full-body panel spanning the combined height of both rows, extending from the top margin to the bottom margin of the sheet. Each panel contains one view of the SAME character. The horizontal gutter between the headshot rows stops at the full-body panel; the full-body panel remains one uninterrupted vertical image. PANEL PLACEMENT: Top left: panel 1, front neutral. Top centre: panel 2, three-quarter neutral. Bottom left: panel 3, side profile neutral. Bottom centre: panel 4, front smiling. Rightmost column, spanning both rows: panel 5, full-body front view. FRAMING: Panels 1-4 share the same portrait scale and head size, with eye height aligned within each row. Panel 5 has its own independent framing: their standing figure fills approximately 94 percent of the full panel height, spanning nearly the entire vertical height of the sheet. Head-size matching and eye-height alignment apply ONLY to the four headshot panels. PANELS 1-4 - FULL-HEAD PORTRAITS: Show their entire head and hairstyle, including the complete hair, with their neck and upper shoulders visible below. Use matching head size across all four portraits and aligned eye height within each row. Keep the lighting and portrait framing consistent across both rows. Determine the shared portrait scale from PANEL 3 FIRST: fit the entire side silhouette, from the tip of their nose to the farthest point of their hair, comfortably inside the panel. Leave empty background on both sides, each margin at least 10 percent of the panel width, and clear space above their hair. Then use that same head size in panels 1, 2, and 4. Make all four heads smaller if necessary to fit every hairstyle silhouette in full. Centre the entire head-and-hair silhouette within each panel. Preserve the hair's shape and length. Their head stays upright in every portrait. TOP ROW - FRONT AND THREE-QUARTER VIEWS, BOTH WITH A NEUTRAL EXPRESSION: 1 - FRONT HEAD PORTRAIT, TOP LEFT: Their face and shoulders point directly toward the camera, with both eyes equally visible and looking toward the camera. Their head is upright and level, with a neutral expression. 2 - THREE-QUARTER HEAD PORTRAIT, TOP CENTRE: They turn 45 degrees toward the left edge of the image. Both eyes remain visible, with the farther side of their face narrower. Their expression is neutral. BOTTOM ROW - SIDE PROFILE AND FRONT SMILING: Panel 3 sits directly beneath panel 1. Panel 4 sits directly beneath panel 2. 3 - STRICT SIDE PROFILE, BOTTOM LEFT, ENTIRE HEAD VISIBLE: They turn a full 90 degrees toward the left edge of the image. Their nose points directly left. Show only the near eye and near cheek, with the nose, lips, and chin forming a clear profile silhouette. The far eye is hidden. Include their entire forehead, crown, chin, back of the skull, and complete hair inside this panel. Leave visible background between their nose and the left border, between their hair and the right border, and above their hair. This is a true side view with a neutral expression. 4 - FRONT, SMILING, BOTTOM CENTRE: Use the same straight-on viewing angle as panel 1, with both eyes equally visible and looking toward the camera. Their head and shoulders face directly forward, upright and level. Give them a clear natural smile, with the corners of their mouth lifted, cheeks raised, and a happy expression in their eyes. Only their facial expression changes from panel 1. PANEL 5 - FULL-BODY FRONT VIEW, RIGHTMOST COLUMN SPANNING BOTH ROWS: Show them standing directly facing the camera with a neutral expression, completely visible from the top of their hair to the bottoms of their feet. Leave a small margin above their head and beneath their feet. Their arms rest slightly away from their torso, hands visible, feet slightly apart. Their entire figure fits inside this panel, so their head is smaller than in panels 1-4. Use the entire height of the rightmost column for this view. Enlarge their entire figure proportionally until it fills approximately 94 percent of the panel height. Place the highest point of their hair about 3 percent below the top edge and the bottoms of their feet about 3 percent above the bottom edge. Their figure stretches from near the top of the sheet to near the bottom of the sheet. Preserve natural body proportions. Centre them horizontally, keeping their entire body, hands, hair, and feet inside the panel. Keep their facial identity, hairline, hairstyle, jewelry, skin tone, and clothing consistent across every view. Use a plain light-grey studio background, soft even lighting, sharp detail, and narrow clean gutters between panels. No written labels, extra panels, overlapping figures, cropped heads, cropped hair, or cropped feet. The camera is locked off and static; the scene holds still with no camera motion.
